issues.description: The proposal includes hallucinated business context not found in the Client Matrix, including revenue figures (~$85M), growth metrics (40% following two acquisitions), and a fabricated peer reference (Cascade Freight).
issues.suggested_fix: Remove all hallucinated metrics, growth narratives, and peer references. Restrict the background context strictly to the facts provided in the Client Matrix.

issues.description: The section contains multiple hallucinated technical details, such as 'React Native mobile app (last updated in 2023)', 'maintained internally by 2 engineers', 'Sales Cloud', and 'Excel exports for BI reporting'.
issues.suggested_fix: Delete these fabricated technical specifics. Describe the architecture and pain points using only the provided details (e.g., custom Rails app, Salesforce, NetSuite, driver app).

issues.description: A high-confidence technical risk is missing: 'Previous internal attempts to fix the workflow have failed twice.' Omitting this misses critical context regarding the client's technical debt and risk profile.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a point acknowledging the past failed internal attempts and explicitly state how the proposed modular approach mitigates the risks that derailed those previous efforts.

issues.description: The proposal definitively commits to a '6-month roadmap' (which aligns with a Q3 delivery if starting in March). Because the Q3 vs. Q4 delivery timeline is explicitly marked as 'contradicted' in the Client Matrix, it cannot be stated as a definitive factual plan in the core proposal.
issues.suggested_fix: Soften the language in the timeline section to present the 6-month roadmap as an 'illustrative timeline' or 'proposed scenario', explicitly noting that the final schedule is pending executive alignment on the Q3 vs. Q4 target.

issues.description: The proposal hallucinates a specific stakeholder name and title ('Rajiv Mehta, Head of Compliance') who does not exist in the Client Matrix.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the fabricated name and refer generally to 'Northwind's compliance leadership' or 'the internal compliance team'.

risks: Rampant hallucination of financial metrics, technical specifics, and stakeholder names severely undermines the credibility of the firm and would embarrass the team in front of the client.

The client has deep, fundamental internal disagreements on budget caps, technical strategy (SaaS vs. incremental), and delivery timelines. Proposing a definitive structure before these are resolved risks alienating key decision-makers (e.g., Marcus vs. Sarah/Rita).
